items.sentence: Its sturdy trunk supports a spreading crown, with major limbs branching outward to create a broad canopy.
Many species bear deeply lobed leaves with rounded or pointed tips and a network of visible veins.
Mature bark often develops thick ridges and furrows, though its texture varies among species and with age.
A dense root system extends belowground, with lateral roots helping anchor the trunk in surrounding soil.
Wind carries pollen between flowers in spring, before fertilized flowers develop into acorns later in the growing season.
Deciduous kinds shed their leaves in autumn, then produce fresh foliage when warmer conditions return.
Acorns fall from branches as they ripen, and some are buried by animals that later retrieve or forget them.
New shoots lengthen during favorable growing seasons, while growth slows during cold weather or drought.
These trees occur across much of the Northern Hemisphere, inhabiting environments from cool forests to warm Mediterranean landscapes.
Many grow in mixed woodlands alongside other broadleaf species, forming part of layered forest canopies.
Some species thrive in open, sunny sites, where their wide crowns can develop without close competition.
Several kinds tolerate dry summers and rocky soils, especially in regions with seasonal rainfall.
Long-lived specimens store carbon in woody tissues and soils, contributing to the regulation of atmospheric carbon.
Fallen leaves decompose into organic matter, returning nutrients to woodland soils.
Branches and cavities provide nesting and shelter sites for birds, insects, and small mammals.
The dense hardwood is used in flooring, furniture, barrels, and other durable wood products.
